notes.s: A failure replayed so often it stops feeling familiar.
notes.t: A subunit track for Jin, J-Hope and Jungkook on Map of the Soul: Persona, and the album's darkest three minutes. The conceit is a video game: a run lost, a screen flashing game over, the wish that you could load a save instead of living with it. Underneath it is the specific fear of a performer who has made the same mistake before and cannot get numb to it. The title is the inverse of deja vu and names a real sensation, the moment something you have done a thousand times turns alien, and the Korean lyric uses the clinical Korean term for it outright.
k: 미시감 is the standard Korean term for jamais vu, built as not-yet-seen-feeling against 기시감, already-seen-feeling, for deja vu. The English title is a translation of a word the Korean lyric says plainly, so Korean listeners get the thesis of the song and English listeners get a French loan they have to look up.
-(으)면 되다 means it's enough to do that, the pattern behind I could just reload. Pair it with -(으)면 안 되다, must not, and you have two of the most used constructions in spoken Korean.
The same word contrasted against itself with -지만. Korean does this far more readily than English, and it marks a feeling the speaker refuses to resolve rather than a contradiction he has missed.
오만 is fifty thousand, used as a vague huge number the way English says a million. Korean exaggeration counts in tens of thousands, so 오만 가지 is roughly a million different things.
